title: The pluperfect: what had already happened

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the pluperfect *había salido* from B1 Unit 1: *había* + past participle says that something had already happened before another moment in the past (*el tren ya había salido*). In the story of a coup, it gives the background: what had happened before the military took power.

items.spanish: Allende había ganado las elecciones de 1970.
items.english: Allende had won the elections of 1970.

items.spanish: Cuando los militares tomaron el poder, el país ya había pasado por meses de crisis.
items.english: When the military took power, the country had already gone through months of crisis.

items.spanish: Allende se había quedado en La Moneda con otras personas.
items.english: Allende had stayed in La Moneda with other people.

items.spanish: Los Chicago Boys eran economistas que habían estudiado en la Universidad de Chicago.
items.english: The Chicago Boys were economists who had studied at the University of Chicago.

sections.content: *Ya*, *todavía no* and *antes de* often signal the pluperfect. Nothing goes between *había* and the participle, and *había* agrees with the person: *había ganado*, *habían estudiado*.
